title: Robinson Crusoe
author: Daniel Defoe
desc: 船難後獨自在荒島生活二十八年：蓋房子、種穀物、養山羊，從零打造一個家。

intro: I've been rereading 'Robinson Crusoe.' It's almost a manual for building a life from scratch.
我最近在重讀《魯賓遜漂流記》。它幾乎是一本從零打造生活的手冊。

q: After the shipwreck, Crusoe salvages timber, tools, and gunpowder before the ship breaks apart. With one trip back to the wreck, what would you prioritize?
船難後，魯賓遜在船解體前搶救了木材、工具和火藥。如果只能回沉船一趟，你會優先拿什麼？
o: Tools, without question. Everything else follows.
毫無疑問是工具。其他的都會隨之而來。
without question = 毫無疑問。follow = 隨之而來。
Crusoe agrees. He values a carpenter's chest more than a shipload of gold.
魯賓遜同意。他認為一箱木匠工具比滿船黃金更有價值。
Food and fresh water first.
先拿食物和淡水。
fresh water = 淡水（相對於海水）。
Sensible. His very first raft carries biscuits, rice, and cheese.
很理智。他的第一趟木筏就載了餅乾、米和起司。
Books and paper, to keep my sanity.
書和紙，以保持神智清醒。
sanity = 理智、神智清醒。
Insightful. His journal is what keeps him mentally afloat.
有見地。他的日記就是讓他精神上不沉沒的東西。

q: He builds his dwelling against a rock face and surrounds it with a double palisade. Would you rather live in a cave or build a hut on the beach?
他背靠岩壁建造住所，外面圍了兩層木柵欄。你寧願住洞穴，還是在海灘上蓋小屋？
o: A cave. It's naturally insulated and sturdy.
洞穴。它天然隔熱又堅固。
insulated = 隔熱的。sturdy = 堅固的。
Good engineering instinct. Caves stay cool by day and warm at night.
很好的工程直覺。洞穴白天涼爽、晚上溫暖。
A hut. I'd want the sea breeze and the view.
小屋。我想要海風和景色。
breeze = 微風。
Lovely, though Crusoe would warn you about storms and unexpected visitors.
很美，不過魯賓遜會警告你暴風雨和不速之客。
Both: a cave for storms, a hut for daily life.
兩個都要：洞穴避暴風雨，小屋過日常生活。
A for X, B for Y 是很簡潔的對照句型。
That's exactly what he ends up with: his fortified 'castle' and his 'country house.'
那正是他最後擁有的：他加固過的「城堡」和他的「鄉間別墅」。

q: It takes him months to make a single table and chair, since he has to split each board from a whole tree. What piece of furniture could you not live without?
他花了好幾個月才做出一張桌子和一把椅子，因為每塊木板都得從整棵樹劈出來。你家裡哪件家具是你不能沒有的？
o: A decent mattress. Sleep is non-negotiable.
一張像樣的床墊。睡眠沒得商量。
decent = 像樣的。non-negotiable = 沒得商量的。
Hard to argue with. Crusoe sleeps in a hammock for years; I'd be miserable.
很難反駁。魯賓遜睡吊床睡了好幾年；我會很痛苦。
A proper desk to write at.
一張可以好好寫字的書桌。
proper = 像樣的、合適的。write at a desk = 在桌前寫字。
Same as Crusoe! The table matters most to him because of his journal.
跟魯賓遜一樣！桌子對他最重要，因為他要寫日記。
A sofa for reading.
一張看書用的沙發。
for + V-ing 表示用途。
A true reader's answer. Comfort is underrated in survival stories.
真正讀者的答案。生存故事裡的舒適感常被低估。

q: Over 28 years, the island becomes his home. Where do you personally feel most 'at home,' and why?
28年間，這座島成了他的家。你個人在哪裡最有「家」的感覺？為什麼？
o: In my hometown, surrounded by familiar faces.
在我的家鄉，身邊都是熟悉的面孔。
hometown = 家鄉。surrounded by = 被…圍繞。
People make a place home. His isolation only ends when Friday arrives.
是人讓一個地方成為家。他的孤立直到星期五出現才結束。
Wherever my books and my bed are.
只要有我的書和我的床，哪裡都是。
wherever = 無論哪裡。
A portable definition of home. Very modern!
可攜帶的「家」的定義。很現代！
Honestly, I'm still searching for that place.
老實說，我還在尋找那個地方。
still = 仍然。search for = 尋找。
A thoughtful answer. Crusoe resisted the island for years before accepting it.
很深思的回答。魯賓遜也抗拒了這座島好多年才接受它。

end: Fascinating. Next time, let's talk about how he feeds himself.
很精彩。下次來聊他怎麼養活自己。

intro: Let's move on to food. Crusoe's diet on the island is surprisingly varied.
我們接著聊食物。魯賓遜在島上的飲食出奇地多樣。

q: He accidentally discovers barley and rice growing where he'd shaken out an old grain sack. Have you ever grown your own food?
他意外發現大麥和稻米長在他抖掉舊穀袋的地方。你自己種過食物嗎？
o: Just herbs on my balcony, like basil and mint.
只在陽台種香草，像是羅勒和薄荷。
herbs = 香草。basil = 羅勒（九層塔的近親）。mint = 薄荷。
That counts! Fresh herbs completely transform a dish.
那也算！新鮮香草能徹底改變一道菜。
Yes, my grandparents have a vegetable plot.
有，我祖父母有一塊菜園。
vegetable plot = 菜園。
Wonderful. There's nothing like eating something you harvested yourself.
太棒了。沒有什麼比吃自己收成的東西更好。
No, I'd probably kill every plant.
沒有，我大概會把每株植物都種死。
probably = 大概。
Ha! Crusoe's first crop fails too, because he sows it in the dry season.
哈！魯賓遜第一次也失敗了，因為他在乾季播種。

q: It takes him nearly a year to bake his first loaf, because he has to make a mortar, a sieve, and an oven from scratch. Which everyday food do you take most for granted?
他花了將近一年才烤出第一條麵包，因為研缽、篩子和烤爐都要從零做起。你最視為理所當然的日常食物是什麼？
o: Rice. We eat it every day without thinking.
米飯。我們每天吃都沒多想。
without thinking = 不假思索。
And yet every bowl represents months of labor. Crusoe would appreciate that.
然而每一碗都代表數月的勞動。魯賓遜會懂這一點。
Bread from the corner bakery.
街角麵包店的麵包。
corner bakery = 街角的麵包店。
After reading his ordeal, I'll never complain about the price of a baguette again.
讀了他的艱辛後，我再也不會抱怨法國麵包的價格了。
Salt, honestly.
老實說，是鹽。
honestly 放句尾 = 說真的。
An underrated answer. Preserving meat without salt would be a nightmare.
被低估的答案。沒有鹽要保存肉類簡直是惡夢。

q: He domesticates wild goats for milk, butter, and cheese. Could you ever raise animals for food?
他馴化野山羊來取得奶、奶油和起司。你能飼養動物來當食物嗎？
o: Chickens for eggs, maybe. Not for meat.
也許養雞下蛋。但不是為了吃肉。
A, maybe. Not B. 是很簡潔的讓步句型。
A thoughtful compromise. Many urban farmers do exactly that.
深思熟慮的折衷。很多都市農夫正是這麼做的。
No, I'm vegetarian.
不行，我吃素。
vegetarian = 素食者。
Then you'd rely on his grapes. He sun-dries them into raisins, you know.
那你就得靠他的葡萄了。你知道嗎，他會把葡萄曬成葡萄乾。
If I had to survive, yes.
如果為了生存，會。
If I had to = 如果我不得不。假設語氣用過去式。
Survival changes priorities quickly. The novel is honest about that.
生存會很快改變優先順序。這本小說對此很誠實。

q: By the time the rescue ship arrives, he's stored enough dried food for years. Do you keep a well-stocked pantry, or shop day by day?
救援船抵達時，他已經囤了好幾年的乾糧。你會把食物櫃塞滿，還是天天買？
o: My pantry could survive a siege.
我的食物櫃撐得過一場圍城。
siege = 圍城。誇飾的幽默說法。
Crusoe would hire you immediately!
魯賓遜會立刻雇用你！
Day by day. I like fresh ingredients.
天天買。我喜歡新鮮食材。
day by day = 一天一天地。ingredient = 食材。
That's the joy of city living. Crusoe didn't have a night market.
這就是城市生活的樂趣。魯賓遜可沒有夜市。
Somewhere in between: instant noodles for emergencies.
介於兩者之間：泡麵以備不時之需。
somewhere in between = 介於兩者之間。for emergencies = 以備急用。
The universal emergency food! Very practical.
全世界通用的應急食物！很實際。

end: I'll never look at a loaf of bread the same way. Thanks for the chat!
我再也不會用同樣的眼光看待一條麵包了。謝謝你陪我聊！
